18	- Keep top-level `old`/`new` as optional for backward compatibility.

The tool description names the common case of a definition plus its uses. This applies to any multi-location bug in any codebase and does not depend on the model following a 'same turn' instruction it has already ignored.

154	def _edit_ignoring_whitespace(target: Path, path: str, text: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:
155	    """Fallback when `old` has no exact match: match line by line ignoring surrounding whitespace,
156	    re-indent `new` to fit, or explain precisely how `old` differs from the file."""
157	    old_lines = old.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
158	    file_lines = text.split("\n")
159	    stripped = [line.strip() for line in file_lines]
160	    want = [line.strip() for line in old_lines]
161	    n = len(old_lines)
162	    hits = [i for i in range(len(file_lines) - n + 1) if stripped[i : i + n] == want]
163	    if len(hits) > 1:
164	        starts = ", ".join(str(i + 1) for i in hits)
165	        raise ValueError(f"`old` matches (ignoring whitespace) at lines {starts}; include more surrounding context")
166	    first = next((k for k, w in enumerate(want) if w), None)
167	    if not hits:
168	        match = difflib.get_close_matches(want[first], stripped, n=1, cutoff=0) if first is not None else []
169	        if not match:
170	            raise ValueError("`old` not found in file; re-read the exact lines and copy them verbatim")
171	        line_no = stripped.index(match[0])
172	        actual, mine = file_lines[line_no], old_lines[first]
173	        raise ValueError(
174	            f"`old` not found. Closest line in the file is line {line_no + 1}: {actual!r} "
175	            f"(leading spaces: {_indent(actual)}); your first line was {mine!r} (leading spaces: {_indent(mine)}). "
176	            "Copy the text exactly as shown."
177	        )
178	    i = hits[0]
179	    delta = 0 if first is None else _indent(file_lines[i + first]) - _indent(old_lines[first])
180	    new_lines = new.rstrip("\n").split("\n") if new.rstrip("\n") else []
181	    if delta > 0:
182	        new_lines = [" " * delta + line if line.strip() else line for line in new_lines]
183	    elif delta < 0:
184	        new_lines = [line[min(-delta, len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))) :] for line in new_lines]
185	    file_lines[i : i + n] = new_lines
186	    target.write_text("\n".join(file_lines), encoding="utf-8")

content.text:
I made the 'Chosen fix' change in `mend/worker.py`, and no other file was touched. I didn't run anything, as you asked, so the change hasn't been tested yet.

- **Tool definition:** `edit_file` now takes an `edits` list, where each item has a required `old` and `new` and the list needs at least one item. The single top-level `old`/`new` still works for older calls, and `path` is the only required field.
- **Tool description:** it still has the exact-match, uniqueness and line-prefix rules and the automatic-test note. It now adds the three sentences from the diagnosis about putting the whole fix in one call.
- **Applying edits:** the file is read once and each edit is applied in order to the text in memory. The rules for zero, one or several matches are the same as before. The file is written only after every edit succeeds, and the result has one summary line per edit.
- **No-match fallback:** the whitespace-tolerant helper now takes the text and returns the new text plus a note, instead of writing the file itself. Its errors are unchanged except for an `edit k: …; nothing was written` prefix. `k` starts at 1.

The agent loop is unchanged.
